Helpers for code that drops the class

Source: R/vctrs.R
zu_ifelse.Rd

Base functions that build their result from the values without their class, such as ifelse() and vapply(), read a zuint vector's raw bits as numbers. These helpers do the same jobs and keep the type.

Usage

zu_ifelse(test, yes, no)

zu_vapply(X, FUN, FUN.VALUE, ...)

Arguments

test

A logical vector.

yes, no

Values for TRUE and FALSE, recycled to test.

X

A vector or list.

FUN

A function.

FUN.VALUE

A zuint or decimal128 vector of the length each result must have.

...

More arguments to FUN.

Value

A zuint vector.

Details

zu_ifelse() takes yes and no to their common type (see zu_common_type()) and is NA where test is. zu_vapply() calls FUN on each element of X and requires each result to have the length of FUN.VALUE, a zuint prototype such as int64(0); the results take its type. Both take decimal128() vectors too: zu_ifelse() combines yes and no as c() does, and zu_vapply() converts each result to the type of FUN.VALUE as x[i] <- value does, exactly or NA.

Base functions that cannot dispatch

R dispatches most functions on their first argument only, and some read a vector's payload without dispatching at all. Design 4.1 accepts that cost. Each function below returns the raw bits of the values, or drops their class, so the answer is wrong, often with no warning. For decimal128 the bits are the scaled coefficients.

  • c() and rbind() of data frames with a non-zuint first argument or first column: c(1L, int128(5)) is complex bits, as is rbind(data.frame(x = 1L), data.frame(x = int128(5))). Put the zuint vector first, or use vctrs::vec_rbind() or dplyr::bind_rows().

  • sum(), min(), max(), range() and the other Summary functions read only the first argument's class: sum(int128(5), 1L) is exact and sum(1L, int128(5)) reads the raw bits. Put the zuint vector first.

  • is.unsorted(): use is.unsorted(xtfrm(x)), whose ranks are exact.

  • complete.cases() reads the payload's NaN patterns, so its answer is inverted for negative int64 values: use !is.na(x) on each column.

  • aggregate() and rowsum() read the payload, as a group or as the values. A negative int64 group vanishes. Group by as.character(x), and sum each group with zu_vapply(split(x, g), sum, x[0]).

  • var() and cor() read the payload: var(int64(1:10)) is 0. Use var(as.double(x)), which rounds to a double. sd() is right.

  • unlist(), sapply() and vapply() drop the class. Use do.call(c, list) and zu_vapply().

  • ifelse(): use zu_ifelse().

  • formatC() and sprintf("%f") read the bits (sprintf("%d") is an error). Use format(), as.character() or format_hex(); paste() and sprintf("%s") are right.

  • A zuint vector as an index or a count of a base function that does not dispatch on it: letters[int64(2)], rep(1, int64(3)), rep_len(), seq_len(), numeric() and vector() are empty, and an int128 index is an error. Pass as.integer(i). A zuint vector as the vector being indexed, or as rep()'s x, is right.

  • base::matrix(), base::array(), base::outer() and diag() return the raw bits. zuint vectors do not form matrices, and the functions that dispatch refuse them with a zuint_unsupported_error: %*%, base::crossprod() and base::tcrossprod() (the last two from R 4.4.0), cbind(), rbind(), as.matrix(), aperm() and scale().

  • base::match(), %in%, base::table(), merge() and the set functions compare a bare double as text: see zu_match().

  • cut() has a method: see zu_cut.

Padding data frames and data.table

Base R fills new rows with its own NA, whose bits are a valid int64, uint64, int128 or uint128 value. Growing a data frame by row (d[nrow(d) + 2, "id"] <- 7L, through xpdrows.data.frame()) strips the class and fills the new rows of every zuint column with that value, not NA. The same holds for data.table's rbindlist(fill = TRUE), d[c(1, NA)], shift() and := NA on uint64, int128 and uint128 columns, and a data.table by groups the NA of a uint64 column with its neighbouring value (bit64 pads int64 in base data frames the same way). No zuint method is reached.

These pad correctly: rbind() of data frames with a zuint first column, merge(), vctrs::vec_rbind() and dplyr::bind_rows(). With data.table, fill and join on as.character() of the column, or convert the column after the operation. An int64 column works natively in data.table.

Examples

x <- int64(c("-9223372036854775807", "5", NA))
zu_ifelse(x > 0L, x, int64(0))
#> <int64[3]>
#> [1]  0  5 NA
zu_vapply(1:3, function(i) uint64(2)^i, uint64(0))
#> <uint64[3]>
#> [1] 2 4 8
